newsitem.title: USA: U.S. and Russian space crews resupply Mir.
newsitem.headline: U.S. and Russian space crews resupply Mir.

text.p: American and Russian space crews worked aboard their linked spaceships on Sunday, continuing the orbital resupply of Russia's Mir space station, a NASA official said.

The crews of U.S. space shuttle Atlantis and the Russian space station had moved more than 100 items onto Mir since the two craft docked on Friday night, said Frank Culbertson, who oversees NASA's joint missions with Russia.
"When the shuttle and Mir come together, you end up with one crew that works very well," he said at a news conference on Sunday.
The astronauts and cosmonauts were on schedule to complete some three tons of deliveries by the time the shuttle uncouples from Mir on Wednesday evening, he said.
Bags and boxes containing food, clothing and other equipment floated back and forth between the shuttle's cargo carrier and the sprawling Russian space complex.
The shuttle's deliveries included repair kits for Mir's leaking cooling system and ailing life support systems. A replacement oxygen generator was among the first items to be moved across to Mir.
"They've got the things they need to continue the mission and continue the repair work if it becomes necessary," Culbertson said.

NASA's Jerry Linenger, who was relieved from duty by British-born astronaut Michael Foale, had to contend with a string of mechanical breakdowns and a flash fire during his four-month stay aboard Mir.
The space station's fortunes appeared to turn around with the arrival in April of an unmanned resupply ship carrying repair gear. Most of malfunctioning systems were successfully restored to health.

"As you can see, I'm alive and healthy, smiling, so the condition of the station is the same. We practically have no problems," Mir commander Vasily Tsibliev told CBS radio in an interview broadcast from space on Sunday.
Shuttle commander Charles Precourt added that he was "very satisfied" with the health of the space station, where NASA's Foale is to spend four months.
Atlantis, which is making its sixth visit to Mir, is due back at its Florida spaceport on Saturday morning.
Linenger is looking forward to his return to Earth and a reunion with his infant son, John, and his wife, Kathryn, who is expecting their second child in June.
"He's real happy to be coming home with us," Precourt said.
